public_rationale: On May 25, 2022, Neyshabur reported that adding “on back of” or “on shoulders of” improved Imagen’s chance of depicting a horse riding an astronaut [e5]. The demonstration does not separate wording effects from learned plausibility preferences, so it cannot establish whether those preferences contributed to the original failure [e5]. The claim that common sense played no causal role remains unresolved [e5].
limitations: The demonstration provides no repeated-sample success rates or controlled comparison separating wording from scene plausibility [e5].
Successful rewording establishes neither the presence nor the absence of a plausibility-based contribution to the original failure [e5].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Imagen's failure on 'a horse riding an astronaut' was not due to common sense.

statement.excerpt: And, no, it wasn’t about common sense at all.

from_speaker: it wasn’t about common sense at all
our_interpretation: The claim concerns the cause of original Imagen’s May 2022 failures on the horse-riding-astronaut prompt.
In context, “common sense” means a plausibility judgment or learned expectation that makes the model favor ordinary riding arrangements.
Successful rewording can rule out an absolute inability or unconditional refusal. It does not by itself rule out a contributing plausibility preference.
The categorical phrase “at all” requires stronger evidence than showing that wording affects the result.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled comparisons or model interventions show that plausibility-based judgment did not cause the original failure, while identifying a sufficient alternative mechanism.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled evidence shows that a plausibility-based judgment or expectation causally contributed to the role reversal.

evidence.explanation: The researcher reports improved success after specifying the riding position. This challenges an unconditional refusal explanation, but does not isolate or exclude a contributing preference for plausible scenes.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled tests on original Imagen, using repeated samples and matched prompt variants, that separate wording from plausibility effects.
